A1.justification: Both PDFs describe In Search of Adam’s Secret Sauce. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training experiments on SlimPajama and Fineweb, optimizer comparisons with validation perplexities, and simulations on quadratic problems.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds experiments without gradient clipping, with a doubled token budget, and with a generalized variance-based optimizer.

M1.justification: v2 Sections 4.2 and C.4 introduce and evaluate AdaVar, allowing separate momentum, variance-smoothing and variance-scaling parameters β, τ and γ. v1 considered the generalized expression theoretically but did not deploy it as this optimizer family. The central equal-beta Adam procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use SlimPajama and Fineweb language modeling, homogeneous and heterogeneous quadratic problems, and synthetic gradient-signal demonstrations. The added experiments vary training budgets and optimizer settings within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The original Table 1 comparator roster is unchanged. Figure 20 newly compares the tied, Adam-equivalent configuration with untied AdaVar variants, including variants with γ = 1; these comparison variants were not experimentally evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 6.4B-token, 12,400-step training condition, an Adam control without global gradient clipping, and AdaVar parameter sweeps. Existing evaluation protocols remain intact. The 420M-to-410M figure-caption correction agrees with v1’s existing model specification in Appendix A.2 and does not establish a model change.

E4.justification: Three substantial analyses extend the checks on the central recommendation: removing Adam’s gradient clipping (Figure 12), doubling training tokens (Figure 13), and independently varying the generalized variance update’s parameters (Figure 20). These test whether equal-beta performance depends on preprocessing, training duration or the restricted optimizer parameterization.

E5.justification: The three-initialization-seed means and two-sigma intervals in the tables, and the ten-seed medians and quartiles for quadratic experiments, are retained. The added hyperparameter sweeps introduce no documented change to repeated-seed or uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial result sets in Figures 12, 13 and 20: equal betas remain competitive without clipping, at twice the token budget, and within AdaVar’s broader parameterization. Figure 12 identifies β1 = β2 = 0.9 as its best tested setting. Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results; the additions do not constitute improvements to those same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Equation 4 changes the KL coefficient from λ to 1/λ, resolving its mismatch with Theorem 4.1’s β = 1/(1+λ) and the existing appendix derivation. Appendix C.3 makes the substitution explicit. The central propositions, theorem and equal-beta necessity result are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims that Adam outperforms the studied simplifications, equal betas are often near-optimal, and this setting admits a variational-inference interpretation. Updating the abstract from over 1,300 to over 1,500 trained models expands the supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets AdaVar’s results as further evidence that strong performance aligns with the theoretically motivated tied parameters. Figure 12 also qualifies the no-clipping findings: higher β2 can help at particular fixed β1 values, while jointly tuning equal betas remains effective. The conclusion’s existing limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendices A.1.1 and A.1.2 add learning-rate and beta grids, run counts, clipping settings and training-step information for the new experiments. Appendix C.4 specifies AdaVar’s update and links its experimental setup to Figure 2. Hardware, architecture and code/data access information otherwise remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Alacaoglu et al. (2020), Zhang et al. (2022), and Xie and Li (2024) when discussing theoretical beta constraints. It expands the comparison with Balles and Hennig into Section 4.2 and softens the assertion that newer optimizers’ gains depend on Adam.

P1.justification: The Balles–Hennig discussion moves into an expanded subsection, new experimental subsections are inserted, and the variational proof receives additional explanation. Local wording, cross-references, author information and publication headers are updated. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the multi-panel Figures 12, 13 and 20. Existing figures are locally repositioned and renumbered, and the 410M-model plot gains dashed equal-beta reference annotations. The original tables and most graphical displays retain their structure.

improvement.justification: The added clipping, training-budget and AdaVar analyses strengthen support for the equal-beta recommendation, while the Equation 4 correction improves consistency between the stated objective and theorem. Clearer discussion of prior work also helps establish the contribution. These are useful incremental gains over v1’s already extensive study; the main findings and acknowledged limitations remain largely unchanged.
